title: Insecure API
description: Security training API demonstrating OWASP API vulnerabilities and secure coding patterns

preview.what: An intentionally vulnerable API system with insecure and secure implementations.
preview.why: Built to make OWASP API risks easier to test, explain, and fix.
preview.focus: API security testing, secure coding patterns, and CI/CD security checks.

caseStudy.context: Insecure API is a security training API that demonstrates common OWASP API vulnerabilities alongside safer implementation patterns.
caseStudy.problem: API security issues are easier to understand when developers can see the insecure behavior, test it directly, and compare it with a secure version.
systemDesign: The project is structured as an intentionally vulnerable API with routes that demonstrate common API security failures.
Secure implementation examples sit alongside vulnerable patterns so the difference is visible in code and behavior.
The repository includes CI/CD security pipeline integration to show how automated checks can support API security work.

title: M-Pesa Simulator
description: Offline replica of M-Pesa Daraja APIs for testing payment workflows

preview.what: An offline simulator for M-Pesa Daraja API payment flows.
preview.why: Built to test payment integrations without relying on live payment infrastructure.
preview.focus: Payment API behavior, callback handling, and integration testing.

caseStudy.context: M-Pesa Simulator is an offline replica of M-Pesa Daraja APIs used to test payment workflows in a controlled local environment.
caseStudy.problem: Payment integrations need repeatable testing for callbacks, request states, and failure handling before they touch real payment systems.
systemDesign: The simulator models payment API behavior so developers can test integration flows locally.
It supports workflow testing around request creation, API responses, and payment callbacks.
The project helps separate payment-flow testing from production credentials and live transaction dependencies.

title: iOS Security
description: iOS application security auditing scripts and guides

preview.what: A repository of iOS application security auditing scripts and guides.
preview.why: Built to support repeatable iOS security review and testing workflows.
preview.focus: Mobile app auditing, testing notes, and practical security checks.

caseStudy.context: iOS Security collects scripts and guides used for iOS application security auditing and mobile review workflows.
caseStudy.problem: Mobile security testing benefits from repeatable checks, documented workflows, and tooling that keeps audits consistent.
systemDesign: The repository groups iOS security scripts and reference notes around practical audit tasks.
Guides are organized to support repeatable testing instead of one-off manual checks.
The structure is meant to help security review move from setup into evidence collection faster.

title: Frida Scripts
description: Runtime instrumentation scripts for Android security testing

preview.what: A collection of Frida scripts for Android runtime instrumentation.
preview.why: Built to inspect app behavior while the application is running.
preview.focus: Runtime analysis, tamper testing, SSL pinning checks, and Android behavior inspection.

caseStudy.context: Frida Scripts contains runtime instrumentation scripts used during Android security testing and behavioral analysis.
caseStudy.problem: Static review does not always show how an Android app behaves during execution, especially around runtime checks and tamper controls.
systemDesign: The repository organizes Frida scripts around common Android testing tasks.
Scripts are written to hook methods, inspect runtime behavior, and support repeatable mobile testing.
The project supports faster setup for runtime analysis during Android application assessments.
